india_plate_position: EarthByte 40.5S, 68.6E; PALEOMAP 48.1S, 58.4E; modelled distance to the Eurasian reference point 2,676 km (EarthByte), 4,517 km (PALEOMAP)
collision_status: No collision. India is part of Gondwana, far south of Eurasia.
tectonic_process: Gondwana is assembled; Neo-Tethys opens along its northern margin.
mountain_building_context: No Himalayan mountain system. The region is a Gondwanan continental margin.
geological_evidence: Plate reconstructions place the Indian Plate at high southern latitudes next to Antarctica and Australia.
uncertainty: Reconstructions disagree on the position of India by thousands of kilometres this far back.

tectonic_process: Gondwana is still joined; rifting begins to affect its margins later in the Jurassic.
geological_evidence: Reconstructed position of the Indian Plate within Gondwana.
uncertainty: Model dependent; no direct geological observation of the position.

india_plate_position: EarthByte 43.5S, 52.3E; PALEOMAP 34.9S, 42.4E; modelled distance to the Eurasian reference point 9,733 km (EarthByte), 7,672 km (PALEOMAP)
tectonic_process: East and West Gondwana are separating; India is still attached to Antarctica and Australia.
geological_evidence: Reconstructed position and published plate models.
uncertainty: The configuration of eastern Gondwana varies between models.

india_plate_position: EarthByte 46.4S, 56.5E; PALEOMAP 41.3S, 45.0E; modelled distance to the Eurasian reference point 9,884 km (EarthByte), 8,055 km (PALEOMAP)
tectonic_process: India begins to separate from Antarctica and Australia and to move northward.
geological_evidence: Seafloor spreading in the Indian Ocean recorded in published plate models.
uncertainty: Timing of separation differs by several million years between models.

india_plate_position: EarthByte 42.7S, 53.5E; PALEOMAP 41.5S, 47.7E; modelled distance to the Eurasian reference point 9,538 km (EarthByte), 7,866 km (PALEOMAP)
collision_status: No collision. A wide Neo-Tethys ocean lies between India and Eurasia.
tectonic_process: Northward motion of the Indian Plate across the Indian Ocean region.

collision_status: No collision. The modern Himalaya does not exist.
tectonic_process: Indian Plate moves northward through the Indian Ocean region.
mountain_building_context: No Himalayan mountain system. The northern margin of India faces Neo-Tethys.
geological_evidence: Reconstructed plate position and paleogeographic maps.

india_plate_position: EarthByte 21.4S, 56.3E; PALEOMAP 26.1S, 63.0E; modelled distance to the Eurasian reference point 6,636 km (EarthByte), 5,074 km (PALEOMAP)
tectonic_process: Rapid northward motion continues; the Deccan region is still south of the equator in the model.

india_plate_position: EarthByte 12.9S, 58.8E; PALEOMAP 17.0S, 66.7E; modelled distance to the Eurasian reference point 5,658 km (EarthByte), 4,274 km (PALEOMAP)
collision_status: No collision in most reconstructions. The ocean between India and Eurasia is narrowing.
tectonic_process: Deccan flood volcanism on the Indian Plate; continued northward motion.
geological_evidence: U-Pb ages of the Deccan Traps; reconstructed plate position.
uncertainty: Whether any contact with Asia existed this early is argued by a minority of authors.

india_plate_position: EarthByte 0.1N, 64.4E; PALEOMAP 2.9S, 70.4E; modelled distance to the Eurasian reference point 4,124 km (EarthByte), 3,021 km (PALEOMAP)
collision_status: Collision onset is debated; estimates for first contact range from about 65 to 35 Ma, with 60 to 50 Ma commonly favoured.
tectonic_process: India approaches the southern margin of Eurasia; convergence rates are high.
mountain_building_context: Collision-related deformation has not yet produced the modern Himalayan relief.
geological_evidence: Palaeomagnetic convergence histories, sedimentary provenance and ophiolite emplacement.
uncertainty: No single agreed date; the range reflects different criteria for 'collision'.

india_plate_position: EarthByte 6.6N, 65.3E; PALEOMAP 2.5N, 72.0E; modelled distance to the Eurasian reference point 3,328 km (EarthByte), 2,427 km (PALEOMAP)
collision_status: Initial contact between the Indian margin and Asia is proposed for around this time by several models; others place it earlier or later.
tectonic_process: Convergence continues; crustal shortening and deformation begin to affect the Indian margin.
mountain_building_context: Early stages of Himalayan-Tibetan mountain building; not the modern range.
geological_evidence: Sedimentary provenance changes, high-pressure metamorphism and palaeomagnetic data.
uncertainty: One of several competing estimates; see the collision events.

collision_status: Collision-related deformation is under way in published models.

mountain_building_context: A developing Himalayan-Tibetan mountain system, much lower and narrower than at present in most interpretations.
geological_evidence: Foreland basin sedimentation and metamorphic ages.

tectonic_process: Ongoing shortening and exhumation of Himalayan rocks.
uncertainty: Timing of uplift of individual ranges is debated.

uncertainty: Details of elevation history are debated.
